footer.about: Open-source Open Banking infrastructure built for the needs of Vietnamese banks, released under the Apache 2.0 license.
footer.disclaimer: The project is at an early stage and the API specification is a draft. Legal documents referenced on this site should be checked for validity and content before official use.
home.title: VOBS — Open-source Open Banking infrastructure for Vietnamese banks
home.description: An open-source Open Banking stack that fits the needs of every bank in Vietnam and can be customized to each bank's systems. It helps banks comply with Circular 64/2024/TT-NHNN without exposing their core banking systems: API gateway, consent, integration hub, VietQR, ISO 20022.
home.ogDescription: Open-source Open Banking infrastructure that fits the needs of every bank in Vietnam, following Circular 64/2024/TT-NHNN.
home.lead: VOBS ships what every bank needs to roll out Open APIs under Circular 64/2024/TT-NHNN: a FAPI 2.0 API gateway, consent management, an integration hub that syncs data from the core, plus VietQR and ISO 20022 libraries. Because it is open source, each bank tailors it to its own systems without exposing its core. Fintechs reach every bank through the same API.
home.fact.coverage: Basic Open APIs from Article 6 covered by the spec
home.fact.license: Committed never to relicense the core
home.problem.h2: Every bank is solving the same problem
home.problem.lead: Banks must expose APIs to a common standard, but their core systems were never designed for it. The work is the same at every bank and gives none of them a competitive edge.
home.problem.c1.h3: Circular 64 sets the standard and the deadline
home.problem.c1.p: A catalogue of basic Open APIs, consent capped at 180 days, limits on automated queries, logs kept for at least 3 months, systems at security level 3.
home.problem.c2.h3: Legacy cores cannot take Open API traffic
home.problem.c2.p: T24, Flexcube and Silverlake run end-of-day batches, cap throughput and charge by license to scale. Pointing read APIs straight at the core puts every partner's load on it.
home.problem.c3.p: Each bank has its own API style and onboarding process, so integration cost grows with every bank instead of being reused.
home.problem.c4.h3: Consent must be explicit and traceable
home.problem.c4.p: Vietnam's Personal Data Protection Law (No. 91/2025/QH15) and Data Law require consent that is scoped, time-limited and revocable, with every access on record.
home.arch.h2: Reads and writes take separate paths
home.arch.lead: Read requests are served from a read store that the integration hub keeps in sync with the core, so core load does not grow with the number of partners. Writes such as payment initiation go through the bank's own systems; VOBS never writes to the core through a back door.
home.arch.alt: VOBS architecture: third parties call the API gateway; reads come from a read store synced from the core by the integration hub; writes go through the bank's payment hub to the NAPAS and MDP switches
home.arch.legendRead: Read path: never touches the core
home.modules.h2: Ten modules, each usable on its own
home.modules.lead: A bank can take only the ISO 20022 library, or only the consent module, and adapt it to the systems it already runs. Infrastructure comes from mature open-source projects; VOBS focuses on what is specific to Vietnam. The label on each module shows how ready it is today.
home.tt64.lead: Every API in the specification names the clause of the Circular it implements, so banks can trace each one during rollout and compliance reviews.
home.tt64.callout: Compliance deadline. Banks already connected to third parties must fully comply with the Circular by this date (Article 15). The detailed technical specifications in Appendices 01 and 02 have not been cross-checked yet; see the mapping page for which parts are VOBS design choices.
home.tt64.groupA: Exchange rate and interest rate APIs (point a)
home.tt64.groupB: Consent, access token, account and transaction history APIs (point b)
home.tt64.groupC: Payment initiation, e-wallet top-up and withdrawal APIs (point c), for banks and payment intermediaries only
home.audience.bank.p: Meet the deadline without overloading the core, tailor the stack to your current systems, and cut license costs and vendor lock-in. Runs on-premise.
home.audience.fintech.p: One API style and one onboarding process across every bank running VOBS; try it first in a sandbox generated from the same specification.
home.audience.si.p: A ready-made platform to deploy for banks, instead of rebuilding from scratch on every project.
home.audience.regulator.p: A standard implemented consistently across banks; being open source, anyone can check how each requirement of the Circular is met.
home.cta.h2: Open source from day one, auditable from day one
home.cta.p: Licensed under Apache 2.0. Releases are signed and ship with an SBOM, and every dependency passes a license check, so banks can assess supply-chain risk. Report bugs, comment on the specification or contribute connectors on GitHub.
tt64.title: Circular 64 mapping — VOBS
tt64.description: How the VOBS API specification maps to the basic Open API catalogue in Article 6 of Circular 64/2024/TT-NHNN, and how VOBS meets its rules on consent, rate limiting and logging.
tt64.lead: Circular 64/2024/TT-NHNN of the State Bank of Vietnam governs Open APIs in the banking sector and took effect on March 1, 2025. Banks already connected to third parties must fully comply by March 1, 2027. VOBS spec {{SPEC_VERSION}} covers {{TT64_COVERED}}/{{TT64_TOTAL}} APIs from the Article 6 catalogue; the table below maps each API to its endpoint in the specification.
tt64.catalog.lead: Select an endpoint to open it in the spec. APIs under point c may only be offered to third parties that are banks or licensed payment intermediaries (Article 5). API names below are English translations; the Vietnamese page shows the original names.
tt64.catalog.footnote: * Vietnamese name back-translated from the English version; not yet matched against the original. The two "update authentication status" APIs are modelled as webhooks the bank calls on the third party; that direction is a VOBS design to be checked against Appendix 01.
tt64.group.a: Point a — Exchange and interest rates
tt64.translatedNote: Vietnamese name not yet matched against the original
tt64.provisions.h2: Other requirements and how VOBS meets them
tt64.pending.p1: Appendix 01 (technical specification of each API) and Appendix 02 (architecture, data and security standards) have not been cross-checked. Paths, field names, error codes and authentication requirements in the spec are currently VOBS design choices based on international practice: OpenAPI 3.1, OAuth 2.0, FAPI 2.0, RFC 9457.

api.title: API specification {{SPEC_VERSION}} — VOBS

api.note: Draft {{SPEC_VERSION}}: API catalogue follows Article 6 of Circular 64/2024/TT-NHNN; paths and fields not yet checked against Appendix 01. Descriptions inside the spec are in Vietnamese.

infra.title: Reference infrastructure and cost — VOBS
infra.description: Reference infrastructure and cost for deploying VOBS at three sizes, on-premise and in the cloud: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, Viettel IDC, CMC Cloud, FPT Cloud, VNG Cloud.
infra.h1: What it takes to run VOBS
infra.lead: Three reference sizes, from a pilot to a large bank, with on-premise and cloud costs. Each size covers a production site, a DR site and non-production environments. List prices as of {{INFRA_AS_OF}}, at {{INFRA_USD_VND}} VND per USD, before VAT. Use the figures for early budgeting, not in place of quotes.
infra.fact.places: places to run production while customer data stays in Vietnam: on-premise, Vietnamese clouds, the AWS Hanoi Local Zone
infra.fact.onpremM: five-year cost of a two-site on-premise setup at medium size, the lowest of all options
infra.fact.small: five-year cost at small size: three-year cloud commitments and on-premise come out about even
infra.load.lead: Pick the size closest to the bank's expected load, then adjust to real figures.
infra.load.footnote: Each call returns 4 KB to the partner on average and writes 1 KB of compressed audit log. Audit logs are kept for one year on write-once (WORM) storage.
infra.sites.lead: Each site is one Kubernetes cluster across 3 failure domains, with an app node pool for stateless services and a data node pool for Kafka, PostgreSQL, Valkey and observability. The DR site keeps the full data pool and half of the app pool.
infra.sites.footnote: Node counts are the sum of component resources times 1.3, rounded up to a multiple of 3. At size L the PostgreSQL read store runs on 16 vCPU/128 GB nodes, each counted as 2 data nodes.
infra.components.footnote: Each cell is replicas × vCPU/RAM, plus data disk per replica. Keycloak follows the official sizing guide: about 120 client credentials grants per second per vCPU, plus 150% headroom.
infra.where.lead: Production with customer data belongs where the data stays in Vietnam. Kafka, PostgreSQL and Valkey run on Kubernetes through operators everywhere, so the setup is the same on-premise and in every cloud.
infra.where.onprem: On-premise (the bank's data centers or colocation)
infra.where.onprem.k8s: Self-run: RKE2, kubeadm or a commercially supported distribution
infra.where.aws.vn: Yes, one zone, live since June 2026
infra.where.aws.fit: Production; the DR site goes elsewhere in Vietnam
infra.where.local.k8s: CMC Kubernetes, FPT Kubernetes Engine, VNG VKS
infra.where.local.fit: Production, DR, or the DR site for on-premise
infra.where.global.vn: Not yet; Singapore is the nearest
infra.where.global.fit: Sandbox, development, load testing; production only if legal approves transferring data abroad
infra.where.footnote: Circular 09/2020/TT-NHNN allows banks to use third-party cloud, with conditions on system classification, provider selection and backup plans. The bank's legal team should confirm each choice.
infra.cloud.lead: USD per month for production, DR and non-production together, before VAT. Virtual machines make up about 53–77% of the cost; SSD disks come second.
infra.cloud.quoteOnly: No published VM prices; request a quote using the sizing table
infra.cloud.footnote: VMs: m7i/r7i.2xlarge (AWS; the Hanoi Local Zone matches Singapore prices), D8s/E8s v5 (Azure), n2-standard/n2-highmem-8 (Google Cloud, after sustained use discount), ecs.g7/r7.2xlarge (Alibaba), T2.Gen 06 and T2.Mem Burst 03 packages (Viettel IDC). CMC Cloud prices are interpolated from its Kubernetes node price list. Three-year commitments have no upfront payment; Alibaba and Vietnamese clouds discount long-term contracts by quote. Carrier circuit fees are not included.
infra.onprem.lead: Two sites: the main site runs production and non-production, the DR site has as many servers as production. Figures in USD.
infra.onprem.footnote: Hardware prices are assumptions to replace with quotes: a 2U server at about USD 25,000 (S: 2 × 16 cores, 256 GB) and USD 50,000 (M, L: 2 × 32 cores, 512 GB), including 5-year warranty and the 2025–2026 rise in server memory prices. Add 3 control plane servers and about USD 40,000 of network gear per site. A 42U rack in a Tier III data center is taken at VND 30 million per month (list prices VND 20–42 million). All software is open source, with no license fees.
infra.tco.lead: Thousand USD, excluding operations staff. Bars compare against the most expensive option at the same size.
infra.tco.footnote: Cloud uses three-year commitment prices, renewed at the same rate. Alibaba Cloud and Vietnamese clouds use monthly list prices, so the gap narrows with long-term quotes. On-premise needs a team for hardware, Kubernetes and stateful systems, about 3 people at size S to 6 at size L; cloud removes the hardware part.
infra.excluded.hsm: HSM: VOBS uses the bank's existing HSM over PKCS#11 and only needs a new partition. A new HSM or a cloud HSM is priced by quote.
infra.excluded.links: Circuits to the bank's data center, cross-connect fees, Internet for on-premise sites.
infra.excluded.audit: Independent penetration tests, information system security level assessment, PCI DSS certification where needed.
infra.excluded.tools: Security tools the bank requires on every node: SIEM, PAM, vulnerability scanning.
infra.excluded.tax: VAT, and foreign contractor tax on foreign cloud services.
infra.sources.details: Detailed assumptions and the method are in the infrastructure document on GitHub (Vietnamese).
